report_name: Japan Declares First-Ever Cybersecurity State of Emergency After Massive Attacks

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: Used in a large-scale ransomware attack against cloud services provider IDC Frontier, which led to cascading failures for its clients and the exposure of personal data.

attack_patterns.name: Supply Chain Compromise
attack_patterns.description: A ransomware attack on cloud provider IDC Frontier caused a cascading failure, impacting 495 of its downstream business clients in a supply chain-style compromise.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
attack_patterns.description: Implied by the exposure of personal data of around 14 million people and the observation of large data transfers from the cloud provider's network to malicious domains.

tools.name: AI-driven tools
tools.description: Used by threat actors to overcome language barriers and more effectively target Japan's legacy infrastructure.

campaigns.name: October 2026 Japan Cyberattacks
campaigns.description: A wave of crippling cyberattacks in September and October 2026 targeting Japanese businesses, notably cloud provider IDC Frontier, which led to a national cybersecurity state of emergency.
campaigns.objective: Disruption of services and data theft from Japanese businesses.

identities.name: Japanese government
identities.description: Declared its first-ever 'cybersecurity state of emergency' in response to a wave of cyberattacks impacting hundreds of businesses and millions of citizens.

identities.name: National Cybersecurity Strategy Headquarters (NCSH)
identities.description: The Japanese government body that made the decision to declare the cybersecurity state of emergency.

identities.name: IDC Frontier
identities.description: A cloud services provider owned by SoftBank that was the victim of a major ransomware attack, leading to a supply-chain compromise of 495 of its clients.

identities.name: SoftBank
identities.description: Owner of the compromised cloud provider, IDC Frontier.

identities.name: 495 business clients of IDC Frontier
identities.description: Downstream businesses impacted by the ransomware attack on their cloud provider, IDC Frontier.

indicators.name: Ransomware File Encryption Pattern (.locked)
indicators.pattern:
title: Ransomware File Encryption with .locked Extension
id: 2b9a7c3d-1e8f-4b9a-8c7d-6e5f4d3c2b1a
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of files with a '.locked' extension, a common pattern for ransomware observed in attacks in Japan.
references:
  - https://www.cpomagazine.com/cyber-security/string-of-ransomware-cyber-attacks-prompts-first-cybersecurity-state-of-emergency-declaration-from-japan/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
  - attack.t1486
  - attack.impact
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate applications that may use this extension for lock files, though uncommon as a final file extension.
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.locked'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects files being renamed with a '.locked' extension, a common indicator of ransomware activity mentioned in the cyber observables.
